title: Small Stock Pre- and Post-slaughter Procedures in an Abattoir;

lessons.title: Pre-slaughter work in the lairage
lessons.html:
Your work experience

In this module you work in the lairage and in the post-slaughter areas of a sheep and goat abattoir, with a mentor. You do the real work, and your mentor signs your logbook when you can do it correctly.

Receiving animals

  1. Check the documents: owner, number of animals, and proof of ownership.
  2. Count the sheep and goats as they come off the truck.
  3. Compare the count and marks with the documents. Report differences.
  4. Look for dead, injured, lame or sick animals and report them to the supervisor and meat inspector.
  5. Off-load calmly with the ramp. No throwing, dragging or kicking.

Lairage care

  • Pen animals by owner without overcrowding.
  • Make sure every pen has clean water.
  • Keep the lairage record: pen, owner, number, time of arrival.
  • Move animals the meat inspector sets aside at ante-mortem inspection to the suspect or isolation pen.
  • Clean pens after they are emptied, as the schedule says.

Moving to slaughter

  • Move small groups quietly through the race.
  • Use a flag or rattle. Do not hit animals.
  • Do not overfill the race.
  • Keep the order of slaughter as the supervisor plans it, so that each owner's animals stay together on the kill sheet.

What you learn

You will learn how a normal, healthy sheep or goat stands, walks and breathes, so that you notice the ones that are not normal. This is an important skill for a slaughterer.

lessons.title: Post-slaughter work
lessons.html:
Tasks after dressing

Once the carcasses have been dressed and inspected, you help with:

  • Inspection decisions: passed carcasses continue; detained ones go to the detain rail when the inspector says; condemned material goes to the locked condemned area.
  • Final trimming and washing of carcasses.
  • Weighing and recording carcass number, owner and mass.
  • Presenting carcasses to the classifier and for stamping.
  • Chilling: hanging carcasses with space between them, closing doors, recording temperatures.
  • Offal: chilling red offal and tripe, keeping them separate.
  • Skins: taking skins to the skin store and salting or stacking them as your plant does.
  • Dispatch: loading carcasses into clean, cold trucks and completing dispatch notes.

Working hygienically after slaughter

  • Clean hands and clean clothing when handling chilled carcasses.
  • Carcasses never touch the floor, walls or each other.
  • Skin-store workers do not enter the chillers without changing and washing.

Safety

  • Use the rails to move carcasses; do not carry many at once.
  • Wear warm clothing in the chiller and non-slip boots.
  • Know how to open the chiller door from the inside.
  • Salt for skins can hurt your eyes and cracked skin; wear gloves.

lessons.title: Evidence for your logbook
lessons.html:
What your mentor looks for

TaskYou show that you
ReceivingCount, check documents and report problems
LairageHandle animals calmly and make sure they have water
Inspection decisionsHandle passed, detained and condemned material correctly
WeighingRecord correct numbers and masses
ChillingSpace carcasses and record temperatures
DispatchLoad hygienically and complete documents

Writing your logbook

  • Each day, write the date, the area and what you did.
  • Use simple, clear sentences. Example: 'Received 85 sheep from one farmer. Counted 85. One lame ewe reported to supervisor and moved to suspect pen by inspector.'
  • Attach copies of records you completed, if your training provider allows it.
  • Ask your mentor to sign after watching you.

Problems you must always report

  • Animal numbers or marks that do not match the documents.
  • Injured, sick or dead animals.
  • Pens without water.
  • A warm chiller or open door.
  • A dirty truck at dispatch.
  • Any injury.

Reporting a problem quickly is a sign of a competent worker, not a weak one.

Key points

  • Count animals and check ownership documents on arrival.
  • Every pen must have clean water; handle animals calmly.
  • Follow every inspection decision after slaughter.
  • Weigh, chill and dispatch carefully, and record everything correctly.
  • Report problems quickly and keep your logbook signed.
